about.title: Gridley Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Gridley is a small, walkable community, but that doesn't mean property owners get a pass on keeping their spaces safe. Whether the fall happened on a wet floor at a market along Spruce Street, a cracked walkway near Sycamore Street, or an unlit stairwell in a rental unit, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix or warn people about it? That's the heart of a premises liability case. Because Gridley is a tight-knit town, evidence like store surveillance footage or maintenance logs can disappear quickly if no one asks for it. If you were hurt on someone else's property, getting the hazard documented and any video preserved early on matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can look at what happened and explain your options, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Gridley Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition before your fall. An attorney can help track down inspection records, prior complaints, or employee schedules that speak to this.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Gridley businesses and apartment complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you can still recover a portion of damages. An attorney can help explain how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Gridley?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or school, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim notice. Because these timelines are strict, it's worth having a conversation with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell at a small local business and I know the owner?
items.answer: That's a common concern in a community the size of Gridley, but a claim isn't really against the person, it's against their insurance coverage. Business owners generally carry liability insurance for exactly this kind of situation. An independent attorney can help you understand how to move forward without the case feeling personal.

items.question: Do I need proof the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Generally, yes. California premises liability law usually requires showing the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and didn't fix or warn about it in time. Photos of the hazard, witness statements, and any available video can all help build that picture.
